whatsHappening.background: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing one of the world’s largest humanitarian crises. Its roots go back to the Congo wars of the 1990s and early 2000s, when regional armies and armed groups fought across the east. Today, violence is concentrated in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri, where M23, the ADF, local militias, Congolese forces, and regional tensions keep civilians trapped between conflict, displacement, hunger, and weak basic services.

timeline.description: The First and Second Congo Wars draw in neighboring countries and leave eastern Congo unstable.
M23 briefly captures Goma before being pushed back, then later reemerges.
M23 advances again as fighting, displacement, and regional accusations escalate.
M23’s advance around Goma worsens one of the world’s largest displacement and hunger crises.

civilianImpact.experiences: Civilians in Congo face repeated displacement, insecurity, hunger, and limited access to basic services. Families fleeing violence often arrive in overcrowded camps or host communities with little shelter, food, or clean water. Children face missed schooling, malnutrition, trauma, and recruitment or abuse risks, while women and girls face serious risks of sexual violence and exploitation.

whatsHappening.background: Eastern Congo’s conflict falls hardest on civilians who have already been displaced many times. Families flee attacks, then often end up in overcrowded camps or host communities with limited food, clean water, health care, sanitation, and school access. Hunger, disease outbreaks, sexual violence, child recruitment, and funding gaps make survival even harder.

civilianImpact.experiences: The civilian impact is not just about fleeing violence. People who escape attacks often reach places where basic survival is still uncertain. Overcrowded sites may lack safe water, sanitation, and medical care. Children face malnutrition, missed school, and trauma, while families lose livelihoods when fields, markets, and roads are cut off by insecurity.

whatsHappening.background: Helping Congo means supporting civilians living through conflict, displacement, and hunger. Relief organizations provide food aid, emergency shelter, nutrition treatment, safe water, health care, and child protection, but needs remain far greater than available funding.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping Congo does not require solving the entire conflict. It means supporting people who need food, protection, shelter, and medical care right now. Awareness also matters because Congo’s emergency is often overlooked, even as millions remain hungry and displaced.
